result.summary: Do not dispatch this spec yet: its central premise is false, its RED declaration cannot resolve the declared tests, and its prescribed fixture cannot demonstrate the claimed loss.

findings.title: The universal only-copy premise excludes existing failure paths
findings.body: O1 claims every surviving shelf file is an only-copy, but validate.js:1489–1504 explicitly retains duplicates when identity reads fail or the best-effort deletion throws. Repeated preservation of identical content also creates separate filenames without deduplication. One successful-redaction fixture cannot establish this universal property. O5–O8 use that false premise to eliminate alternatives and mandate inaccurate recovery documentation; refused fall-through notes also have no sanitized version promoted to the vault.
findings.recommendation: State that shelf files may be the sole surviving copy, distinguish successful redactions from refused fall-throughs and retained duplicates, and reassess the dependent decisions and documentation against those cases.

findings.title: The RED declaration names a nonexistent nested test
findings.body: expectRed[].test is an outermost-first identity path, not a list of independent tests (scripts/red-proofs.js:694,1599–1602). This declaration therefore identifies R8 nested inside OC-1, although both are top-level tests. The baseline phase will reject it before mutation. Splitting the entries alone is insufficient: R8's existing assertion does not emit the specified O1 signal, and the spec prohibits changing existing tests.
findings.recommendation: Declare two expectRed objects, each with a single-element test path and a diagnostic signal that its assertion actually emits. Update the byte-exact contract and verify the declaration against the runner.

findings.title: The two-run fixture either preserves a duplicate or never triggers pruning
findings.body: RUN defaults to publish:false, so the first prescribed run leaves the original note unchanged. The second run then preserves identical bytes in its own protected shelf copy: deleting R cannot make the O2 absence assertion pass. If the implementer publishes the first run to satisfy O1's scrubbed-vault assertion, the unchanged second run has no secret to redact and cannot trigger pruning. The fixture never introduces distinct secret-bearing content for that second run.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly publish the first run, then introduce a different secret-bearing note before the second run. Assert one completed redaction per run and that the second preserved original differs from R before checking eviction and byte absence.

next_steps: Correct the canonical premise and its dependent documentation.
Repair the fixture and RED declaration before marking the spec Ready.
